title: Death is nothing to us
src: Epicurus, Letter to Menoeceus (Diogenes Laertius X.125) · tr. R. D. Hicks (1925)
author: Epicurus
lines: Death, therefore, the most awful of evils, is nothing to us,
seeing that, when we are, death is not come,
and, when death is come, we are not.
why: The most famous argument against the fear of death, in one sentence: where death is, you are not. Learn it to have the strongest case for not fearing death ready to hand, and then ask whether it answers the fear you actually have, which may be less of being dead than of losing those you love.
